country.leadNote: The highlighted figure is the highest among the countries shown. On planned length and project count that reflects how much is announced and how much of each country is recorded here, not how much has been delivered. Nothing is highlighted when every country ties or when only one has a figure.
country.leadNoteLow: On the delivery rows the lowest figure is highlighted instead: less delay, a smaller overrun and a cheaper kilometre are the better outcome.
country.compareDeliveryNote: Delivery rows are measured only on the sections that record a contract duration or a cost, so they rest on fewer sections than the network rows above. A dash means nothing there could be measured.

rankings.title: Delivery performance
rankings.intro: How infrastructure projects held to their budgets and their timetables. Every figure comes from the contract terms and costs recorded on each section, and a section appears only once the data supports the claim.
rankings.coverage: Measured on {lots} sections: {estimate} with an estimate-to-outturn comparison, {award} against the contract award, {completedSlip} delivered with a contract timetable, {ongoingSlip} still running.
rankings.coverageGap: The gaps are missing data, not clean records. A section without a recorded outturn cost or contracted duration cannot be measured, so it is left out rather than assumed on budget.
rankings.emptySlip: No section yet records both a contracted duration and an anchor date.
rankings.methodologyCosts: Costs carry the price year they were quoted in, and both sides of every comparison are restated into a common year before the percentage is taken, so an estimate made in 2013 is never measured directly against money spent in 2023. Costs recorded in different currencies are restated first and then converted to euro at that year's annual average exchange rate, in that order: converting first would use a rate from one year against prices from another.
rankings.methodologySchedule: Schedule slip uses the contract as the baseline rather than a press announcement, because that is the commitment the public paid for and the only baseline present for sections whose announced dates were never recorded. Negative values mean early.

table.sortHint: Sort by this column. Click again to reverse it, a third time to clear it.

performance.openedHelp: Every section that has opened, and how far past its contract date it ran. Sort by any column.
performance.costHelp: The best cost figure each section has: the outturn where one was published, otherwise the signed contract value, otherwise the pre-tender estimate. To rank them together each figure is restated into common prices and then converted to euro at that year's exchange rate. A section whose currency or price year falls outside those tables keeps its recorded cost but has no comparable figure, and sorts to the bottom.
performance.contractorHelp: Builders only, since a construction overrun belongs to whoever built the thing. Joint-venture work counts toward each partner, and name variants are resolved to one firm. Firms with a single section are left out.
performance.countryHelp: The same measures aggregated by country.
performance.emptyCost: No section yet records a cost figure of any kind.
performance.orderCost: Most expensive per kilometre first until you sort.
performance.orderGroup: Worst median slip first until you sort.

about.title: About
about.lead: A map of how countries actually build: what got finished, when it was promised, and what it cost.
about.dataBody: Sections are the unit that matters: a motorway opens in pieces over decades, and an average across the whole road hides that. Every section carries its own dates, cost, contractors and route, and the figures below are counted from those records.
about.dataSources: Every figure comes from a public source that is cited on the project page. Where a number was never published, the field is left empty rather than filled with a guess, which is why some tables are shorter than you might expect. Routes are drawn from OpenStreetMap.
about.builtNote: Counted from the data files when this page was built, on {date}.
about.helpBody: The data is hand-curated, so gaps and mistakes are normal. Three ways to make it better:
about.helpReport: Spot something wrong or missing? Tell me what and where.
about.helpData: Add a country, a project or a missing cost figure. The data lives as plain JSON files with a cited source on every project.
about.helpSpread: Send it to someone who argues about infrastructure. Most of the interesting corrections come from people who already know the road.

contractors.title: Contractors
contractors.intro: Every firm named on a section: what it built, where, and how that work ran against its contracts.
contractors.metaDescription: The firms that built the sections, with length, countries, schedule slip and cost overruns for each.
contractors.leagueHelp: Firms credited with at least {min} sections, worst median slip first. Measured exactly as on the performance page.
contractors.directoryHelp: All {count} firms named anywhere in the data, most sections first.
contractors.builderOnly: Only construction counts toward these figures. A design contract is listed on the firm's page and never folded in, because a construction overrun belongs to whoever built the thing.
contractors.jointVentureNote: Work done in a joint venture is credited to each member firm, so a venture has no page of its own and never appears beside its members: that would count one section twice.
contractors.registryGap: {unregistered} of {total} firms here match no entry in the contractor registry, so two spellings of one company rank as two firms. That is a gap in data/contractors.json, and every one of them is already a data validation warning.
contractors.unrankedNote: {count, plural, one {# firm is credited with a single section and is} other {# firms are credited with a single section and are}} left out of the league above: one job is not a track record.
contractors.otherRolesHelp: Credited to this firm, counted nowhere above.
contractors.notRankedHere: Too few sections to rank. The figures below describe the work; they are not a track record.
contractors.noDeliveryData: No section this firm built records both a contracted duration and a delivery date, so there is no slip to report.
contractors.noOverrunData: No section this firm built records both an estimate and a final cost.
contractors.measuredOn: Slip measured on {measured} of {total} sections built.
contractors.empty: No firm is named on any section yet.

dataPage.title: Data and API
dataPage.intro: Every figure on this site is compiled from JSON in the repository and served as static files. Those files are public, so the dataset is an API: fetch it, join it, redraw it.
dataPage.metaDescription: The public data files behind the site: endpoints, schemas, licence and build stamp.
dataPage.endpointsHelp: Relative to this site's origin. A path in braces is one file per record; the manifest lists every id.

endpoints.projects: Every project with its sections: dates, lengths, costs, funding, contractors and sources. The schema describes one entry of the projects array.
endpoints.countries: Area and population per country, behind the density figures.
endpoints.cities: Cities that have their own view: population, GDP per person, map centre.
endpoints.contractors: Canonical contractor identities: the aliases that collapse to one firm, and joint-venture membership.
endpoints.deflators: Consumer price indices, used to restate a cost into another price year within its own currency.
endpoints.deflatorsConstruction: The same shape on construction input costs: a closer fit for civil works, covering fewer currencies and stopping earlier.
endpoints.fx: Annual average exchange rates against the euro, applied after deflation and never before.
endpoints.manifest: Which countries, cities and projects have geometry files, plus the build stamp.
endpoints.countryOutlines: Country outlines, the map's click targets. Natural Earth, public domain.
endpoints.cityMarkers: One point per city, with its project and section counts.
endpoints.countryGeometry: Every section in one country, one feature each, carrying the properties the map styles and filters on.
endpoints.cityGeometry: The same for one city's network, which is kept out of the country file.
endpoints.projectGeometry: One project's sections on their own, for embedding a single route.

dataPage.schemaHelp: JSON Schema for the hand-written source files, generated from the zod definitions by npm run data:schema. Point an editor at one and it validates while you type.
dataPage.licenceGeometry: The route geometry is derived from OpenStreetMap and is licensed ODbL. Reusing it means keeping the attribution and releasing derived geometry on the same terms. The endpoints it covers are marked ODbL above.
dataPage.licenceTables: Everything that is not OpenStreetMap geometry, the curated project records and the reference tables, is offered under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Reuse it anywhere, including commercially, as long as you credit the source and say if you changed it:
dataPage.licenceSources: The figures inside come from public sources, and every file names its own in a sources block. Those keep the terms of whoever published them, listed in data/ATTRIBUTION.md in the repository.
dataPage.buildStampNoCommit: Compiled {date}. The build could not read a commit id.
dataPage.csvHelp: The two league tables as CSV, carrying the same figures the performance page shows and ids you can join on.
dataPage.stabilityBody: These are build artifacts, regenerated on every deploy. Field names follow the schema and change with it, and nothing is versioned yet, so pin the commit above if you need a shape that holds still.
